item.title: A Nook of One’s Own: Motherhood, Space, and Medieval Romance
item.description: Surrounded by the bustle of family life, Kirtsy Bolton carved out her own little nook of space to research and write her book. In this blog, Kirsty reflects on both her own experience of claiming a space of her own and the ways mothers occupied and used space within medieval romances. The post A Nook of One’s Own: Motherhood, Space, and Medieval Romance appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.

item.title: Coffee as History: Writing Angola’s Colonial Past
item.description: What can the coffee industry reveal about the history of Angola? Jos Velmer explores African farmers’ active and early role in shaping the coffee economy and how it was increasingly constrained by settler colonialism. The post Coffee as History: Writing Angola’s Colonial Past appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.

item.title: How Artistic Skill Travelled in the Twelfth Century
item.description: In this post, Rose Walker explores how people in the twelfth century found and exchanged skilled craftsmen, revealing how artistic expertise travelled through powerful social networks and shaped some of the most striking artworks of medieval Spain and Portugal. The post How Artistic Skill Travelled in the Twelfth Century appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.

item.title: Black History Month: 6 Books to Read on African American History
item.description: In 2026, Black History Month reaches a powerful milestone—100 years since its beginnings as a weeklong effort to recognize and preserve African American history. From studies of a complex history to the extraordinary Black women leading the way for change, these 6 books from the University of Rochester Press offer an essential window into African American history. item.title: Discovering Wagner’s Philosophy in the Ring
item.description: Michael Steinberg shares how a small Ring Cycle production in Vermont, led him to explore Wagner as more than a composer. By immersing himself in Wagner’s writings he uncovered the philosophical depth behind the Ring which led to his book, The Philosopher’s Ring—Wagner as Thinker and Dramatist. The post Discovering Wagner’s Philosophy in the <I>Ring</I> appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.

item.title: What should you write in alt text?
item.description: Alt text, short for “alternative text,” is a brief written description of an image. It usually isn’t visible on the screen during normal use. Instead, it works behind the scenes to ensure that digital content is accessible to everyone. In this post we'll take a look at how it is used and share tips on writing good alt text for images. The post What should you write in alt text? appeared first on Boydell and Brewer.
